reason: The loop-control change is a small edit to the active path and keeps each tile’s FP32 update order. Reordering FMOPA operations is similarly low scope, but the four tiles are already independent. A guarded next-B prefetch is cheap to test, though its benefit is uncertain. Padding changes the active scratch layout but adds footprint and address work; prior padding results on other paths do not establish an effect here. Transpose fusion avoids full-panel traffic but repeats A reads 16 times per band, so its traffic cost looks high. The two packed-B proposals are near duplicates and both add a full B read, allocation, and 1 MiB of writes; test at most one before considering the other. The A-transpose fusion proposal targets fallback sizes, not the fixed n=512 panel32 path. No proposal has measured results on this active kernel, and noisy historical scores do not establish causality.
